change.intent: Add a user-scoped, thread-scoped remembered approval for Ask First tools. The approval card offers Decline, Approve Once, and Remember Approval without changing Environment or Project policy.
inScope: Atomic persistence of the current decision and remembered tool approval
Thread, actor, tool, and authority binding
Runtime policy resolution for later invocations in the same thread
Thread-lifetime cleanup, invalidation, projection, audit, and full hosted verification
Removal of the Environment Apps Always Approve detour
protected: Environment Automatic, Ask First, and Blocked policy meanings
Per-invocation prepared-call identity and effect audit
Tool-minimum and runtime-strict approvals that cannot be remembered
Exact payload binding for the current approval
Other threads, users, projects, and environments

readinessReason: The product behavior, affected services, versioned stable tool identity, persisted remembered-approval record, and typed Web-to-runtime evidence boundary are settled. Implementation must start from evidence revision b367560 or a verified descendant because the design-artifact worktree was at eaf690d when the analysis was captured.

directImpacts.effect: Add remembered approval as a separate layer after Environment and Project Ask First resolution. It can satisfy an eligible ask but cannot override deny, subject restriction, tool minimum, or explicit runtime strictness.
Replace the optional boolean decision with an explicit decline, approve_once, or remember_approval decision for runtime approvals while preserving compatibility for old interactions.
Persist a remembered approval keyed by organization, thread, authenticated user, stable tool identity, and authority revision in the same transaction as the current exact decision.
Load active remembered approvals for the current actor and thread, carry typed evidence into the runtime, and apply it when preparing later calls.
Render Decline, Approve Once, and Remember Approval whenever an eligible Ask First decision is required. Do not add a separate remembered-approval management surface.

indirectImpacts.effect: Remove approval-card deep links and return-context code whose only purpose is the misleading Always Approve flow. Independent Environment policy management remains.
Carry the same three-way decision and remembered state. Mobile cannot remain a boolean-only approval surface.
A remembered approval must fail closed when descriptor or approval-authority identity changes. Dynamic tools require a stable provider identity before they are eligible.

Requires a PostgreSQL migration, Web deployment, shared protocol/runtime package update, and hosted turn-worker image. CLI, Desktop, and TUI receive compatible shared types but need not persist hosted remembered approvals.
Remember Approval must bind to the prepare-before-wait design. It cannot authorize reconstructed continuation calls or become another resume snapshot.

requiredValidation: Policy matrix proving Environment Automatic, Ask First, and Blocked behavior with and without remembered approval
PostgreSQL transaction test proving remember_approval records the exact current decision and one actor-thread-tool grant atomically
Cross-user, cross-thread, cross-tool, and stale-authority rejection tests
Full hosted path proving first ask, Remember Approval, and automatic later invocations for the life of the thread
New-thread path proving the same tool asks again
Worker-restart and credential-rotation proof using the same remembered approval
Production telemetry proving no new use of the Environment Apps approval-return flow before deletion

contextPack.objective: Implement remembered approval as a user-thread-tool authorization layer beneath Environment Ask First and above exact per-invocation approval.
interfaces: Thread approval decision: decline | approve_once | remember_approval
StableToolApprovalIdentityV1: tool ID, descriptor contract revision, approval-authority revision
RememberedToolApprovalV1: version, record ID, organization ID, thread ID, actor user ID, stable tool identity, source interaction ID, creation time
Thread interaction response envelope and runtime turn payload
runtimeConstraints: Remembered approval never changes Environment or Project policy
Deny, disabled capability, subject restriction, tool minimum, and explicit runtime strictness override remembered approval
Future calls are newly prepared and audited; the original payload binding is never reused
Only the authenticated user who selected Remember Approval can consume it
Tool or approval-authority revision changes invalidate the remembered approval
Remembered approval follows the thread and is deleted with it
allowedActions: Add versioned contracts and additive persistence
Add Web and worker resolution of remembered approval
Add thread-lifetime cleanup and lifecycle projection
Remove old Always Approve detour after compatibility gates pass
prohibitedActions: Do not mutate Environment or Project policy from Remember Approval
Do not key remembered approval by payload or run credentials
Do not let one collaborator's remembered approval authorize another collaborator
Do not bypass tool minimum, subject restriction, runtime strictness, or deny
Do not reconstruct a tool call after approval
Do not retain temporary compatibility paths without removal gates

evidence.claim: Ask First tools offer Decline, Approve Once, and Remember Approval; remembered approval acts as automatic for that tool in that thread.
Current policy resolves Environment, Project, subject, tool minimum, and runtime strictness but has no thread remembered layer.
The registry derives tool approval disposition from hosted app policy and descriptor-bound authority.
The Web response is boolean and the approval card renders Deny, Approve Once, and an Environment Apps Always Approve link or disabled button.
The Web API accepts an optional approved boolean and forwards it to the durable interaction resolver.
The durable resolver already owns an atomic transaction for response message, app decision, interaction status, queue state, and turn event.
Thread interactions persist request, response, actor, runtime identity, and lifecycle but no remembered tool approval.
Hosted policy evidence already crosses profile and runtime contracts, establishing a typed host-to-runtime seam.
The worker loads and executes turns under a user identity, which must be corrected to preserve the actual deciding actor.
Current Always Approve navigates to Environment Apps, can change broad policy, and then approves the pending request once.
Mobile also models approval as a binary approve or deny decision.
Descriptor and activation identity already provide the basis for stable tool revision and fail-closed handler behavior.
The selected hosted redesign persists one PreparedToolCallV1 before waiting and removes reconstruction bridges.
